title: Talking about cause and effect
about: Collocations for talking about causes and results: verbs like cause, bring about, spark off, attract and produce, adjectives for causes, effects and outcomes, everyday phrases such as have an effect on or make a bad impression, and the difference between affect and effect.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Affect і effect звучать майже однаково (/əˈfekt/ та /ɪˈfekt/), тому їх плутають навіть носії мови. Affect — дієслово «впливати, зачіпати», без прийменника: it affected me deeply, не affected on me. Effect — зазвичай іменник «вплив, наслідок, дія»: have an effect on sth, side effects. Рідко, в офіційній мові, effect буває дієсловом: effect a change — домогтися змін, здійснити зміни. Підказка: дія (дієслово) — affect, результат (іменник) — effect.

rows: Cold weather has a bad effect on my knees.
This medicine has very few side effects.
The residents' group effected several changes to the bus routes.

items.pattern: cause chaos / havoc (in / on / for sth) · create chaos · play havoc with sth
items.meaning: make a situation very confused and disorganised, so that things stop working normally
items.example: The bus drivers' strike **caused chaos** in the city centre this morning.
more: Our new puppy **caused havoc** in the kitchen while we were out.
Forgetting to book the restaurant **caused chaos** at my sister's birthday: twenty hungry people and nowhere to eat.
items.watchOut: Chaos вимовляється /ˈkeɪɒs/ («кейос»), а не «хаос». «Наробити хаосу» — cause / create chaos; make chaos звучить неприродно. Havoc /ˈhævək/ уживають майже тільки в сталих сполученнях: cause havoc, play havoc with sth (Late nights play havoc with my sleep).

items.pattern: cause (a lot of / serious / little) damage (to sth) · do damage (to sth)
items.meaning: harm something so that it is broken, spoilt or in worse condition
items.example: The hailstorm **caused** a lot of **damage** to the cars parked in our street.
more: Too much sun can **cause** serious **damage** to your skin.
Moths have **caused** a lot of **damage** to my wool jumpers.
items.watchOut: Damage тут незлічуване: a lot of damage, much damage, без -s (damages — компенсація, яку присуджує суд). «Завдати шкоди» — cause damage або do damage (to sth), не make damage. Прийменник — to: damage to the roof, не damage of the roof.

items.pattern: cause (some / great / widespread) alarm / concern (among sb) · give cause for concern
items.meaning: make people worried or afraid that something bad might happen
items.example: Plans to close the village post office have **caused concern** among older residents.
more: A strong smell of gas **caused alarm** in our block of flats last night.
The dog's sudden loss of appetite **caused** us some **concern**.
items.watchOut: «Викликати занепокоєння» — cause concern (або raise concern), не call concern: «викликати» тут не перекладаємо як call. Alarm тут — тривога, страх, а не будильник чи сигналізація.

items.pattern: cause sb (great) anxiety / (a lot of) embarrassment · cause anxiety / embarrassment to sb
items.meaning: make someone feel very worried, or very uncomfortable and ashamed
items.uk: завдавати комусь неспокою / сорому, змушувати когось хвилюватися / ніяковіти
items.example: The long wait for the test results **caused** the whole family **great anxiety**.
more: My little brother **caused me a lot of embarrassment** by singing loudly on the bus.
Losing her passport the day before the flight **caused her great anxiety**.
items.watchOut: Після cause можна поставити два додатки підряд: cause sb anxiety (кому — що), без прийменника перед людиною. Не make sb anxiety. Embarrassment — ніяковість, сором; anxiety /æŋˈzaɪəti/ — сильний неспокій, тривога.

items.pattern: bring about a revolution / transformation (in sth) · bring about change
items.meaning: cause a very big change in something
items.example: Cheap flights **brought about a revolution** in the way people go on holiday.
more: The new head teacher **brought about a transformation** in the school: the kids actually enjoy going now.
Moving to the countryside **brought about** a complete **transformation** in my dad's health.
items.watchOut: Bring about — «спричинити, здійснити» (зміни). Не плутай із bring up (виховувати; порушити тему). Із займенником: bring it about. Revolution тут — переворот у якійсь сфері, а не обов'язково політична революція.

items.pattern: bring about the downfall / collapse of sb / sth
items.meaning: make a person, business or organisation fail completely or lose its power
items.example: Years of gambling **brought about the downfall** of my great-grandfather, who lost the family farm.
more: One silly argument almost **brought about the collapse** of their twenty-year friendship.
Poor management **brought about the collapse** of the local football club.
items.watchOut: Downfall — падіння, крах (людини, уряду, бізнесу). Не плутай з downpour — злива. Collapse /kəˈlæps/ — крах, обвал; так само кажуть про будинок, що завалився, і про людину, яка знепритомніла.

items.pattern: create / raise awareness (of / about sth)
items.meaning: help people to know about and understand a problem
items.example: The charity bike ride helped **create awareness** of heart disease in our town.
more: The school is trying to **raise awareness** about healthy eating among parents.
A local mum gives talks in schools to **raise awareness** of food allergies.
items.watchOut: Найчастіше кажуть raise awareness; create awareness теж правильно. Не make awareness. Прийменник — of або about: awareness of the problem. Від прикметника aware: be aware of sth — знати про щось, усвідомлювати.

items.pattern: create / cause problems (for sb)
items.meaning: make difficulties for someone or something
items.example: The new parking rules are **creating problems** for people who live near the station.
more: Our neighbour's huge trees **create problems** for us: there's no sun in the garden at all.
Lending money to friends can **create problems** between you.
items.watchOut: «Створювати проблеми для когось» — create / cause problems for sb, з for. Make problems уживають рідко; природніше create / cause problems, а розмовне — make trouble (for sb).

items.pattern: spark off (or spark) protests / riots / demonstrations / an argument
items.meaning: suddenly cause angry events such as protests, often after a single event or decision
items.example: The plan to close the village school **sparked off protests** from parents.
more: The new parking charges **sparked off demonstrations** outside the town hall.
A single remark about money **sparked off** a huge argument at dinner.
items.watchOut: Spark off — частіше британське; можна й без off: spark protests. Riot /ˈraɪət/ — заворушення, бунт, а не мітинг (мітинг — rally або demonstration).

items.pattern: spark off (or spark) rumours (about sth / of sth / that …)
items.meaning: make people start telling stories that may not be true
items.example: A 'For Sale' sign outside the café **sparked off rumours** that it was closing.
more: The new car in their drive **sparked off rumours** that they'd won the lottery.
Her sudden trip to Paris **sparked off rumours** about a new boyfriend.
items.watchOut: Rumour — британське написання (американське rumor). «Пускати чутки» — spread rumours; «ходять чутки» — there are rumours / rumour has it that… Не hearings: це слухання (у суді).

items.pattern: attract (a lot of / fierce / widespread) criticism / interest (from sb)
items.meaning: make people criticise something, or become interested in it
items.example: The new shopping centre has **attracted a lot of criticism** from people who live nearby.
more: Her paintings of the harbour have **attracted interest** from galleries in London.
The plan to cut down the old trees in the park **attracted** fierce **criticism**.
items.watchOut: «Викликати інтерес, критику» — attract (або draw) interest / criticism, не call interest: «викликати» тут не перекладаємо як call. Interest у цьому значенні незлічуване: a lot of interest, без -s.

items.pattern: attract (a lot of / wide) support (from sb)
items.meaning: get many people to agree with or help something
items.example: The campaign to save the local swimming pool **attracted support** from all over town.
more: Her idea for a street party quickly **attracted support** from the neighbours.
The petition for a new crossing near the school has **attracted** wide **support**.
items.watchOut: Support тут незлічуване: a lot of support, wide support, без -s і без артикля a. «Здобути підтримку» — attract / win / get support.

items.pattern: produce / have the opposite effect (to what you wanted / intended)
items.meaning: lead to the result that is the reverse of what you wanted
items.example: I told the kids to calm down, but it **produced the opposite effect**: they got even louder.
more: Shouting at a crying baby usually **produces the opposite effect**.
Sleeping pills sometimes **produce the opposite effect** and keep people awake.
items.watchOut: «Дати протилежний ефект» — produce / have the opposite effect, а не make the opposite effect. Effect — іменник (ефект, результат), affect — дієслово.

items.pattern: produce (good / quick / any) results · not produce any results yet
items.meaning: lead to a clear, usually good result
items.example: My new running plan is finally **producing results**: I'm much faster than I was in spring.
more: Calling the council every week eventually **produced results**, and they fixed the streetlight.
The new medicine hasn't **produced any results** yet, but the doctor says to wait.
items.watchOut: «Дати результат» — produce results або get results (We're getting results). Make results не кажуть.

items.pattern: the immediate cause (of sth)
items.meaning: the thing that directly made something happen, just before it happened
items.example: The **immediate cause** of the accident was ice on the road, but the driver was also going too fast.
more: Doctors say the **immediate cause** of his fall was a sudden drop in blood pressure.
The **immediate cause** of the row was a dirty frying pan, but they'd been unhappy for months.
items.watchOut: Immediate тут — «безпосередній», а не «негайний»; instant cause не кажуть (instant — миттєвий: instant coffee). Cause — те, що спричинило подію (the cause of the fire); reason — пояснення, чому так (the reason why I'm late).

items.pattern: the underlying cause / problem / reason (of / for sth)
items.meaning: the real, deeper cause that is not obvious at first
items.example: Her tiredness was only a symptom: the **underlying cause** was a lack of iron.
more: We painted over the damp patch, but we didn't fix the **underlying cause**: a leak in the roof.
Teachers want to understand the **underlying causes** of bad behaviour, not just punish it.
items.watchOut: «Глибинна причина» — the underlying cause (або the root cause); the deep cause звучить неприродно. Не плутай underlying з underlined — підкреслений. Наголос на lie: /ˌʌndəˈlaɪɪŋ/.

items.pattern: reduce / minimise / lessen the impact (of sth on sb / sth)
items.meaning: make the bad effect of something smaller
items.example: We planted a hedge to **reduce the impact** of the noise from the main road.
more: Drinking plenty of water can **minimise the impact** of a long flight.
The school tried to **minimise the impact** of the building work on lessons.
items.watchOut: Британське написання — minimise (американське minimize). Прийменники: the impact of sth on sth — вплив чого на що. Impact як іменник — з наголосом на першому складі: /ˈɪmpækt/.

items.pattern: strengthen / increase the impact (of sth)
items.meaning: make the effect of something stronger
items.example: The photos of the flooded houses **strengthened the impact** of the newspaper report.
more: A short pause before the last line **increases the impact** of a joke.
Good music can **strengthen the impact** of a wedding video.
items.watchOut: Strengthen /ˈstreŋθn/ — дієслово від strong: strengthen the impact. «Посилити» — не strong (це прикметник) і не stronger.

items.pattern: an unexpected / unforeseen outcome · have an unexpected outcome
items.meaning: a result that nobody expected or planned
items.example: Our camping trip had an **unexpected outcome**: we found a lost dog and ended up keeping it.
more: Nobody thought the shy new girl would win the talent show, so it was an **unexpected outcome**.
The cookery course had an **unforeseen outcome**: two of the students got married.
items.watchOut: Outcome — результат, підсумок (переговорів, виборів, матчу), а не «вихід». Unforeseen /ˌʌnfɔːˈsiːn/ — від foresee (передбачати): «непередбачений». Unpredicted трапляється дуже рідко, кажуть unexpected або unforeseen.

items.pattern: the predictable / inevitable outcome (of sth) · the outcome was that …
items.meaning: a result that everyone could see coming, or that could not be avoided
items.example: He didn't open a book all term, so failing the exam was the **predictable outcome**.
more: We tried to drive through London on a Friday afternoon, with the **predictable outcome**: three hours in traffic.
Two stubborn people in one small kitchen: arguments were the **inevitable outcome**.
items.watchOut: Inevitable /ɪnˈevɪtəbl/ — наголос на другому складі. Не плутай predictable (передбачуваний: можна було передбачити) і preventable (якому можна було запобігти).

items.pattern: the positive / beneficial effects (of sth on sb / sth) · have a positive effect on sth
items.meaning: good results or influences
items.example: The **positive effects** of the new cycle lanes were clear within a month: fewer cars and cleaner air.
more: Doctors agree on the **beneficial effects** of a short walk after dinner.
A weekend by the sea had a very **positive effect** on my mood.
items.watchOut: Beneficial /ˌbenɪˈfɪʃl/ — корисний, сприятливий; наголос на fi. Ефект, вплив — effect з e; affect — дієслово.

items.pattern: the negative / adverse effects (of sth on sb / sth) · adverse side effects
items.meaning: bad or harmful results
items.example: Too much coffee can have **negative effects** on your sleep.
more: This medicine has very few **adverse effects**, though some people feel sleepy.
Living next to a busy road can have **negative effects** on children's health.
items.watchOut: Adverse /ˈædvɜːs/ — офіційне «несприятливий, шкідливий»: adverse effects, adverse weather. Не плутай з averse (be averse to sth — бути проти чогось). Side effects — побічна дія ліків.

items.pattern: the direct / inevitable result (of sth) · as a direct result of sth
items.meaning: something that happens straight because of something else, or that could not be avoided
items.example: The traffic jam was a **direct result** of a lorry breaking down on the bridge.
more: As a **direct result** of the new crossing, there have been no accidents outside the school.
Higher prices were the **inevitable result** of the bad harvest.
items.watchOut: Іменник result — з of: the result of bad planning. Дієслово — result in (призвести до) і result from (бути наслідком). «Прямий наслідок» — a direct result, не a straight result.

items.pattern: an indirect / unforeseen result (of sth)
items.meaning: a result that comes in a roundabout way, or that nobody expected
items.example: One **indirect result** of working from home is that I now know all my neighbours.
more: An **unforeseen result** of the cheap tickets was that the museum got too crowded to enjoy.
Better sleep was an **indirect result** of giving up coffee.
items.watchOut: «Побічний наслідок» — an indirect result або a side effect (про ліки); a side result не кажуть. Unforeseen — непередбачений, від foresee.

items.pattern: cause (an) uproar (among sb / over sth)
items.meaning: make a lot of people complain angrily and loudly
items.example: The plan to charge for parking at the hospital **caused an uproar**.
more: When the referee disallowed the goal, it **caused an uproar** in the stadium.
Cutting the library's opening hours **caused uproar** in the village.
items.watchOut: Uproar /ˈʌprɔː/ — обурення, гучне невдоволення багатьох людей. «Викликати обурення» — cause an uproar, не call an uproar. Можна і без артикля: caused uproar.

items.pattern: suffer / face / take the consequences (of sth)
items.meaning: have to deal with the bad results of something you did
items.example: He stayed out all night before the match and **suffered the consequences**: he played terribly.
more: Go out without a coat in this weather and you'll **suffer the consequences**.
If you don't pay the bill on time, you'll have to **face the consequences**.
items.watchOut: «Понести наслідки» — suffer / face / take the consequences, а не carry: дослівне «нести» тут не працює. Consequences /ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/ — наслідки; sequence — послідовність.

items.pattern: have a huge / big / great / profound effect on sb / sth
items.meaning: change or influence someone or something a lot
items.uk: дуже сильно вплинути на когось / щось
items.example: Moving to a new school **had a huge effect on** my daughter's confidence.
more: Lack of sleep **has a huge effect on** your mood.
Living with my grandparents for a year **had a huge effect on** how I see the world.
items.watchOut: «Вплинути на» — have an effect on, з on, не to чи at. З effect зазвичай уживають have, а не make чи give. Effect — іменник; affect — дієслово: It affected me = It had an effect on me.

items.pattern: have a major / big / huge / significant impact on sb / sth · make an impact (on sb / sth)
items.meaning: have a very strong effect on someone or something
items.uk: мати великий (значний) вплив на когось / щось
items.example: The new supermarket has **had a major impact on** the small shops in our village.
more: Our grandmother **had a major impact on** all our lives.
A good coach can **have a major impact on** a young player's future.
items.watchOut: «Великий вплив» — a major / big / huge impact. Principal і chief так не вживають: вони означають «головний» і стоять з the (the chief reason). Прийменник — on: impact on sb / sth.

items.pattern: make / create a good / bad impression (on sb)
items.meaning: make people think badly (or well) of you, especially when they first meet you
items.example: Eating with his mouth open **made a bad impression** on my parents.
more: Our new neighbours **made a good impression**: they brought us a cake on the first day.
A messy front garden can **create a bad impression** when you're selling your house.
items.watchOut: «Справити враження» — make / create an impression (on sb). Produce an impression — книжне й рідкісне, це калька з російського «произвести впечатление». Do an impression — зовсім інше: пародіювати когось (He does a great impression of our teacher).

items.phrase: have a lot of influence on
items.pattern: have (a lot of / a great deal of / considerable) influence on / over sb / sth
items.meaning: be able to change how someone thinks or behaves, or how something develops
items.uk: мати великий вплив на когось / щось
items.example: My older sister **has a lot of influence on** what I wear.
more: Celebrities **have a lot of influence on** what young people eat.
The weather **has a lot of influence on** how many people come to the market.
items.watchOut: Іменник influence — з on або over: influence on sb. А дієслово influence — без прийменника: She influences me a lot, не influences on me. Influence тут незлічуване: a lot of influence.

items.pattern: cause / create a sensation
items.meaning: make a lot of people very excited, surprised or interested
items.example: Grandma's bright pink hair **caused a sensation** at the family party.
more: The ten-year-old who sang at the village fair **caused a sensation**.
When the café started selling cakes shaped like dogs, it **caused a sensation**.
items.watchOut: «Викликати сенсацію, справити фурор» — cause / create a sensation, не call a sensation. Sensation ще означає «відчуття» в тілі: a burning sensation in my throat.

items.pattern: affect sb / sth deeply / badly / seriously · be deeply affected by sth
items.meaning: change how someone feels or lives in a strong way
items.uk: глибоко (сильно) вплинути на когось; глибоко зачепити
items.example: My grandfather's illness **affected** the whole family **deeply**.
more: She was **deeply affected** by the letters her mother had kept for fifty years.
Changing schools three times **affected** him more **deeply** than we realised.
items.watchOut: Affect — дієслово, без прийменника: it affected me, не affected on me. Не плутай з іменником effect. Deeply — про почуття; про здоров'я, урожай, ціни частіше кажуть badly / seriously affected.

items.pattern: effect a change / changes / change (in sth) · formal
items.meaning: make a change happen (formal)
items.example: The parents' group **effected a change** in the school's lunch menu: no more chips every day.
more: The new manager **effected** several **changes** to the menu in her first month.
It took two years of campaigning to **effect a change** in the speed limit outside the school.
items.watchOut: Effect як дієслово — офіційне й рідкісне: effect a change = bring about a change. У розмові частіше кажуть make a change. Affect a change — помилка написання, яку роблять навіть носії.

warmup.uk: Нова кав'ярня викликала великий інтерес у місцевих жителів.
warmup.q: The new café has ___ a lot of interest from local people.
warmup.explain: Викликати інтерес — attract interest (або draw interest). Call — дослівна калька з «викликати».

warmup.q: The storm ___ a lot of damage.
warmup.explain: Завдати шкоди — cause damage (або do damage). Make damage і give damage не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Офіціант справив на нас погане враження.
warmup.q: The waiter ___ a bad impression on us.
warmup.explain: Справити враження — make an impression (on sb). Do an impression — пародіювати когось.

warmup.q: If you don't listen, you'll have to ___ the consequences.
warmup.explain: Понести наслідки — suffer (або face, take) the consequences. Carry — дослівне «нести», тут не працює.

warmup.uk: Переїзд дуже сильно вплинув на нашу родину.
warmup.q: The move had a huge ___ on our family.
warmup.explain: Вплив (іменник) — effect: have an effect on. Affect — дієслово: The move affected our family. Effort — зусилля.

warmup.uk: Друзі мають великий вплив на підлітків.
warmup.q: Friends have a lot of influence ___ teenagers.
warmup.explain: Influence on (або over) sb. А дієслово — без прийменника: Friends influence teenagers.

warmup.uk: Безпосередньою причиною затримки став автобус, що зламався.
warmup.q: The ___ cause of the delay was a broken-down bus.
warmup.explain: Безпосередня причина — the immediate cause. Instant — миттєвий (instant coffee).
Впливати, зачіпати — affect (дієслово). Effect як дієслово — «здійснити» (effect a change), infect — заразити.

A.q: A broken traffic light ___ chaos at the crossroads during rush hour.
A.explain: Наробити хаосу — cause chaos (або create chaos). Make chaos і call chaos — кальки.

A.q: Three months of physiotherapy have finally ___ results: I can walk without a stick.
A.explain: Дати результати — produce results (або get results). Make results і do results не кажуть.

A.q: The new owner's silence about his plans ___ off rumours in the village.
A.explain: Породити чутки — spark off rumours. Put off — відкласти, call off — скасувати.

B.q: Long hours at a desk can have ___ effects on your back.
B.explain: Шкідливий вплив — adverse (або negative) effects. Averse — «який не любить чогось» (be averse to sth), inverse — обернений.

B.q: The school cake sale had an ___ outcome: it raised enough money for a new minibus.
B.explain: Несподіваний результат — an unexpected (або unforeseen) outcome. Unknown — невідомий, unaware — який не знає про щось.

B.q: Packing the night before can ___ the impact of an early start.
B.explain: Зменшити вплив — reduce / minimise the impact. Fall — падати (неперехідне, без додатка), decline — зменшуватися (неперехідне) або відхиляти (пропозицію).

C.q: The singer's surprise visit to the village pub ___ a sensation.
C.explain: Викликати сенсацію — cause a sensation. Call — калька з «викликати».

C.q: The new airport has had a ___ impact on house prices in the area.
C.explain: Великий вплив — a major impact. Principal і chief означають «головний» і так не вживаються.

C.q: The new rule banning ball games in the park ___ an uproar.
C.explain: Викликати обурення — cause an uproar. Do і give тут не працюють.

M.q: The cold weather ___ the tomato plants badly.
M.explain: Вплинути на щось — affect (дієслово, без on). Effect як дієслово — «здійснити», infect — заразити.

M.explain: Домогтися змін — effect changes (офіційно). Affected changes тут — помилка.

M.q: Many families were badly ___ by the floods.
M.explain: Постраждати від чогось — be affected by sth. Inflict — завдати (inflict pain on sb).

example.title: The village bakery
example.uk:
Минулої весни відомий кухар відкрив пекарню в нашому тихому селі. Спочатку вона викликала сенсацію: люди приїжджали здалеку. Черги спричиняли хаос на вузькій головній вулиці, і незабаром пекарня викликала чимало критики з боку сусідів.

Щоб розв'язати проблему, кухар оголосив про плани облаштувати велику автостоянку на лужку посеред села. Це викликало бурю обурення і розпалило протести. Проте протести дали несподіваний результат. Кухар запросив усіх на каву, вислухав людей і відмовився від ідеї з автостоянкою. Його чесність справила гарне враження, і його новий план — місця для велосипедів замість автостоянки — швидко здобув підтримку.

Пекарня дуже сильно вплинула на життя села. Тепер ми всі щоранку зустрічаємося там.
example.en:
Last spring, a famous chef opened a bakery in our quiet village. At first, it [[caused a sensation|c7]]: people drove from miles away. The queues [[caused chaos|a1]] on the narrow high street, and the bakery soon [[attracted a lot of criticism|a11]] from the neighbours.

To solve the problem, the chef announced plans for a big car park on the village green. That [[caused an uproar|c1]] and [[sparked off protests|a9]]. However, the protests had an [[unexpected outcome|b5]]. The chef invited everyone in for coffee, listened, and dropped the car park idea. His honesty [[made a good impression|c5]], and his new plan, a bike rack instead of a car park, quickly [[attracted support|a12]].

The bakery has [[had a huge effect on|c3]] village life. Now we all meet there every morning.
